images.title: Perpendicular diameters make a square
images.purpose: Shows that two perpendicular diameters of a circle join up into a square.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large circle in the centre with two crossing diameters and the four end points joined.
images.exact_structure: One circle with centre O, drawn as a thin dark outline. Two diameters as thick teal (#0072B2) lines: AM vertical, with A at the top and M at the bottom, and PL horizontal, with P on the right and L on the left. A small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) square right angle mark at O. The four points A, P, M and L are joined in that order by thick dark lines, making a square standing on a corner, lightly filled amber (#E69F00). The letters A, P, M, L sit just outside the circle at their points and O sits just below and left of the centre. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Equal diagonals that bisect each other at right angles always make a square.
images.description: Shows that two perpendicular diameters of a circle join up into a square.
images.context: Practice concept: equal radii make the diagonals equal and bisected; the right angle makes APML a square.

image_decisions.why: One circle and its two perpendicular diameters show the square test in its simplest setting.
